## Notes

**Supersedes [Map: Vic.ai-style typed AP surfaces (#177)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/177).** #177's thirty closed decisions are this map's baseline and are cited, not re-decided. Its two open tickets, [Build the five-state processing glyph (#223)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/223) and [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225), are re-parented here. #177 is closed.

**Why a second map.** #177 reached its destination as feature slices bolted onto the old pages, with no ticket owning composition and no in-browser verification, and scored 20/40 ([#224](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/224)). This map charts by *surface*, each ticket owning a whole screen's shape, and every execution ticket closes on detector counts.

**Execution mode.** This map carries execution. Decision tickets resolve first; each spawns an execution ticket; execution tickets close only with `impeccable` run at the four points in CLAUDE.md, in-page detector before/after counts at 1440 and 390 (list and pane-open), and `polish`. Dev-server + seed + headless-Chromium recipe is on #225.

**Design protocol.** Every rendered-surface ticket calls the Skill tool for `impeccable` (sub-command named on the ticket) and `intent`, before the work. Grilling tickets on a surface open with `impeccable critique` of the incumbent and cite the tour screenshot they are matching.

**Vic wins ties, with the tour as the record.** "Does this follow Vic or DocuBite?" defaults to Vic without asking, and the answer is read off `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots — not from memory of the older sections. Grill only what the tour does not settle: DocuBite-only features (Exceptions, Touchless, does-not-move-money, bank statements, institutions), data DocuBite lacks (payment terms, discounts, buyers, entities), and anything that would reverse a #177 decision.

**Documented exceptions to Vic** (decided, do not re-open by "Vic wins ties"): the combined fields+source Detail pane (#179 → #224) with History as its tabs instead of Vic's left panel; the collapsible icon rail instead of Vic's top bar (#224 Q5); DocuBite's palette, type and emerald brand (this map, Q2); Exceptions as its own destination (#192); Touchless keeps its name.

**Settled while charting (grilled 2026-09-15):**

- **Scope is the whole operator app** — queues + Detail pane, Approvals inbox, PO matching in the row, Bill Pay + Payment Batches, Admin, mobile approval. One grammar everywhere.
- **Fidelity is grammar, not skin.** Same layouts, panels, chips, bars, keyboard flow, copy patterns; colour and type stay DocuBite's.
- **Payments never move money.** Bill Pay queue (open bills, terms, countdown, discounted amount over struck-through due) and Payment Batches queue (batch → approve → export file). The transfer stays outside DocuBite, as `preparePaymentRun` does today.
- **Approvals is a destination with two queues**, Invoices and PO Mismatches, each a personal Ready-to-Approve view with the sticky Approve/Reject bar. Exceptions stays separate.
- **Admin adopts Vic's full IA including Companies**: Configuration (per-field Editable/Required/Width, consequence toggles), Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies — one login, many companies, per-entity permissions. This is the one schema-and-auth effort on the map; it is researched before it is grilled.
- **Build order:** shell (#225) → distill (#238) → Approvals → PO matching → Payments → Admin → Mobile.
- **Removal protocol (owner's rule, #237):** nothing is removed from the app without the owner signing off each removal by name on the ticket. Removed features are *unplugged* (CONTEXT.md term), not deleted, so a return is a re-link.

Build the Payments destination: Bill Pay and Payment Batches on the queue shell, with payer accounts, terms, discounts and payment records
---
OPEN
wayfinder:task

---
## Question

Execution of #229 (Bill Pay and Payment Batches). Build on `codex/post-login-ux-implementation`: the **Payments** destination on the #225 Queue-screen shell with two queues, `/payments/bill-pay` and `/payments/batches`, mirroring the Approvals destination (#236).

**Decided on #229 — do not re-decide:**

- **Entities (additive schema only):** `payment_runs` extended into the *Payment batch* (name, comment, submittedById, approvedById/At, rejectedReason, exportedAt/By, paidAt/By, payFromAccountId, currencyCode); new `PayerAccount` (name, bank, last four, currency, default) under Settings › Payments; `Supplier.earlyPaymentDiscountPercent` + `earlyPaymentDiscountDays` beside `paymentTermsDays`; new `InvoicePayment` records (documentId, amount, paidOn, method `batch` | `manual`, batchId, reference, recordedById, removedAt/reason). ADR: `docs/adr/0001-paid-state-derived-from-ledger-then-payment-records.md`.
- **Lifecycle:** Pending approval → Approved → Paid; Rejected (reason required) is terminal and returns the invoices to Bill Pay. No persisted Draft. Download stamps `exportedAt` as a fact shown on the batch, never a state. Member submits; owner approves, rejects, downloads, marks paid; self-approval allowed with "You submitted this batch" on the pane and both facts in the audit.
- **Bill Pay rows:** processing state Approved, not cancelled, not fully paid; rows in a pending/approved batch under the *Scheduled* facet; approved rows without supplier bank details shown, undecidable, "Needs bank details" with a link to the supplier. Columns Supplier · Invoice # · Invoice date · Terms ("2/10 net 30") · Due date + `countdown-badge` (purple *Expires in N days* only inside a real discount window) · Bill total · Currency · Amount to pay (discounted over struck-through due, #188's inline-adjustment component, emerald-700 over slate-500 line-through with sr-only "was") · Pay From. No processing glyph column. Amount to pay editable inline on desktop, 0 < amount ≤ due; read-only on the phone. Bulk bar: **Create batch · Mark as paid · Set Pay From**.
- **Create batch dialog:** name `YYYY-MM-DD-001` editable, optional comment, rows grouped by supplier with per-line remove, footer Bills · Total · Pay From; mixed Pay From or currency splits into one batch per pair and the dialog says so.
- **Payment Batches:** system views Pending approval · Approved · Paid; Rejected under Closed. Columns Created · Submitted by · Due (earliest in the batch, countdown, red when overdue and still pending) · Batch name · Bills · Total · Currency · Pay From. Detail pane (60%, documented exception to Vic's 78% sheet): summary strip, supplier-grouped lines, Audit tab, sticky footer Reject · Approve while pending, Download payment file · Mark batch as paid once approved. Server-confirmed, no optimistic removal, no Undo, no single-key approve. Remove payment record with a reason.
- **Metrics:** Bill Pay carries *Open invoices by age* (the bar from `components/dashboard/aging-summary.tsx`) as one band above the header band, buckets clicking into the filtered queue. Payment Batches carries *Early Payment Savings* only when a supplier has discount terms; otherwise no band.
- **Paid state:** derived — ledger confirmation first, then payment records (Paid / Partially paid), batch membership → Scheduled; the pill says "Paid (recorded)" when the ledger has not confirmed.
- **IA:** one rail item *Payments* after Approvals, badge = batches pending my approval; "Prepare payment run" leaves the Invoices bulk bar and its confirm dialog; Invoices' Approve receipt gains "Approved invoices are ready in Bill Pay". The existing download route stays and serves the batch's file. Empty states: "Nothing to pay. Approved invoices land here." / "No batches yet. Select invoices in Bill Pay to create one."
- **Vocabulary:** CONTEXT.md's Bill Pay, Payment batch, Payer account, Payment terms, Payment record — used verbatim.

**Action Summary (in order):** Intent `specify` → `fortify` → `articulate` → `include`. Impeccable `shape` → `layout` → `clarify` → `harden` → `adapt` → `audit` → `polish`. Read `craft-floor.md` before the first edit; run `impeccable context` once.

**Definition of done:** in-page `detect.js` on both queues at 1440 and 390, list and pane-open, plus the Create batch dialog, before/after counts on this ticket; critique re-run beats the incumbent payment-run flow's score (snapshot named on #229's resolution) and the Invoices 25/40 baseline; `evaluate` health ≥ 80 with every heuristic ≤ 1; migrations additive and reversible; tests on the derived paid state, batch splitting and the eligibility rule; seed at least one supplier with discount terms and a payer account on the dev workspace. Dev-server + seed recipe on #225.


**Inherited from the incumbent critique (13/40, `.impeccable/critique/2026-09-15T23-16-19Z__invoices-prepare-payment-run-incumbent.md`) — fix in this build:** a post-confirm receipt (which rows went into the batch, which were left out and why — `skipped` today lives only in the audit); every failure rendered in place, never thrown to `error.tsx` (`owner_only`, `no_documents_selected`, `no_payable_bills_after_filtering`); `validatePaymentInstructions` actually called so all problems show at once; the Create batch dialog is a Dialog, not `max-w-sm` ConfirmDialog (recap clipped at 344/302px), with focus moved into it; strip copy says eligible for payment, not "Eligible for Approval"; dates and money formatted as the queue formats them (no USD fallback on a ZA file); remittance advices surfaced on the approved batch (built today, discarded by the caller); `revalidatePath` targets the queue the operator is on; cramped-padding on the 12px bulk buttons and the 390 two-row wrap.

---COMMENTS---

1	Map: Make the operator app work like Vic.ai (grammar, not skin)
2	---
3	## Destination
4	
5	DocuBite's authenticated app works the way Vic.ai's does, end to end: **Vic's interaction grammar, DocuBite's skin.** Every operator surface — Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Approvals (Invoices / PO Mismatches), Bill Pay, Payment Batches, and Admin — shares one shell: a full-width 62px queue, one header band (View · Sort · summary filter chips opening a hierarchical facet panel), a bulk action row, and one right-hand Detail pane with a sticky bottom action bar. PO mismatches are resolved on the invoice row with per-cell match glyphs and the tolerance arithmetic in view. Payment runs are batched, approved and exported without DocuBite moving money. Admin is a distinct area (Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies) with multi-company access. Approval works on a phone. Implemented and shipped, measured by Impeccable's in-page detector and a critique score above the 20/40 baseline on every queue.
6	
7	Evidence: the full self-guided tour walked 2026-09-15 — `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/` (DocuBite's own Invoices screen from the same day sits beside them).
8	
9	## Notes
10	
11	**Supersedes [Map: Vic.ai-style typed AP surfaces (#177)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/177).** #177's thirty closed decisions are this map's baseline and are cited, not re-decided. Its two open tickets, [Build the five-state processing glyph (#223)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/223) and [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225), are re-parented here. #177 is closed.
12	
13	**Why a second map.** #177 reached its destination as feature slices bolted onto the old pages, with no ticket owning composition and no in-browser verification, and scored 20/40 ([#224](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/224)). This map charts by *surface*, each ticket owning a whole screen's shape, and every execution ticket closes on detector counts.
14	
15	**Execution mode.** This map carries execution. Decision tickets resolve first; each spawns an execution ticket; execution tickets close only with `impeccable` run at the four points in CLAUDE.md, in-page detector before/after counts at 1440 and 390 (list and pane-open), and `polish`. Dev-server + seed + headless-Chromium recipe is on #225.
16	
17	**Design protocol.** Every rendered-surface ticket calls the Skill tool for `impeccable` (sub-command named on the ticket) and `intent`, before the work. Grilling tickets on a surface open with `impeccable critique` of the incumbent and cite the tour screenshot they are matching.
18	
19	**Vic wins ties, with the tour as the record.** "Does this follow Vic or DocuBite?" defaults to Vic without asking, and the answer is read off `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots — not from memory of the older sections. Grill only what the tour does not settle: DocuBite-only features (Exceptions, Touchless, does-not-move-money, bank statements, institutions), data DocuBite lacks (payment terms, discounts, buyers, entities), and anything that would reverse a #177 decision.
20	
21	**Documented exceptions to Vic** (decided, do not re-open by "Vic wins ties"): the combined fields+source Detail pane (#179 → #224) with History as its tabs instead of Vic's left panel; the collapsible icon rail instead of Vic's top bar (#224 Q5); DocuBite's palette, type and emerald brand (this map, Q2); Exceptions as its own destination (#192); Touchless keeps its name.
22	
23	**Settled while charting (grilled 2026-09-15):**
24	
25	- **Scope is the whole operator app** — queues + Detail pane, Approvals inbox, PO matching in the row, Bill Pay + Payment Batches, Admin, mobile approval. One grammar everywhere.
26	- **Fidelity is grammar, not skin.** Same layouts, panels, chips, bars, keyboard flow, copy patterns; colour and type stay DocuBite's.
27	- **Payments never move money.** Bill Pay queue (open bills, terms, countdown, discounted amount over struck-through due) and Payment Batches queue (batch → approve → export file). The transfer stays outside DocuBite, as `preparePaymentRun` does today.
28	- **Approvals is a destination with two queues**, Invoices and PO Mismatches, each a personal Ready-to-Approve view with the sticky Approve/Reject bar. Exceptions stays separate.
29	- **Admin adopts Vic's full IA including Companies**: Configuration (per-field Editable/Required/Width, consequence toggles), Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies — one login, many companies, per-entity permissions. This is the one schema-and-auth effort on the map; it is researched before it is grilled.
30	- **Build order:** shell (#225) → distill (#238) → Approvals → PO matching → Payments → Admin → Mobile.
31	- **Removal protocol (owner's rule, #237):** nothing is removed from the app without the owner signing off each removal by name on the ticket. Removed features are *unplugged* (CONTEXT.md term), not deleted, so a return is a re-link.
32

34	
35	<!-- one line per closed ticket -->
36	- #230 (research): Workspace is already the Company (71/80 models keyed on workspaceId, one Bigcapital org per workspace, nothing above it); one login/many companies already works via per-workspace `WorkspaceMember.role`, the grouping is what is missing; both isolation layers key on `workspace_id`, so Companies should be an additive `Organization` + nullable `Workspace.organizationId` + `OrganizationMember`, with `WorkspaceMember` the only grant of entity access — [docs/research/multi-company-access.md](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/blob/research/multi-company-access/docs/research/multi-company-access.md); eight open decisions handed to #231.

New `models/approvals.ts` (actor-scoped, deduped Ready-to-Approve count for the rail badge), `lib/approvals/row-eligibility.ts`, `startApprovalOnInvoice`/`sendReviewTaskBackForReview`/`cancelApprovalOnDocument`; `SplitPane` gained `initialTab`/`fieldsReadOnly` (locks fields while any stage is pending, in every Detail pane). Map: Make the operator app work like Vic.ai (grammar, not skin)
---
## Destination

DocuBite's authenticated app works the way Vic.ai's does, end to end: **Vic's interaction grammar, DocuBite's skin.** Every operator surface — Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Approvals (Invoices / PO Mismatches), Bill Pay, Payment Batches, and Admin — shares one shell: a full-width 62px queue, one header band (View · Sort · summary filter chips opening a hierarchical facet panel), a bulk action row, and one right-hand Detail pane with a sticky bottom action bar. PO mismatches are resolved on the invoice row with per-cell match glyphs and the tolerance arithmetic in view. Payment runs are batched, approved and exported without DocuBite moving money. Admin is a distinct area (Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies) with multi-company access. Approval works on a phone. Implemented and shipped, measured by Impeccable's in-page detector and a critique score above the 20/40 baseline on every queue.

Evidence: the full self-guided tour walked 2026-09-15 — `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/` (DocuBite's own Invoices screen from the same day sits beside them).

## Notes

**Supersedes [Map: Vic.ai-style typed AP surfaces (#177)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/177).** #177's thirty closed decisions are this map's baseline and are cited, not re-decided. Its two open tickets, [Build the five-state processing glyph (#223)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/223) and [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225), are re-parented here. #177 is closed.

**Why a second map.** #177 reached its destination as feature slices bolted onto the old pages, with no ticket owning composition and no in-browser verification, and scored 20/40 ([#224](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/224)). This map charts by *surface*, each ticket owning a whole screen's shape, and every execution ticket closes on detector counts.

**Execution mode.** This map carries execution. Decision tickets resolve first; each spawns an execution ticket; execution tickets close only with `impeccable` run at the four points in CLAUDE.md, in-page detector before/after counts at 1440 and 390 (list and pane-open), and `polish`. Dev-server + seed + headless-Chromium recipe is on #225.

**Design protocol.** Every rendered-surface ticket calls the Skill tool for `impeccable` (sub-command named on the ticket) and `intent`, before the work. Grilling tickets on a surface open with `impeccable critique` of the incumbent and cite the tour screenshot they are matching.

**Vic wins ties, with the tour as the record.** "Does this follow Vic or DocuBite?" defaults to Vic without asking, and the answer is read off `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots — not from memory of the older sections. Grill only what the tour does not settle: DocuBite-only features (Exceptions, Touchless, does-not-move-money, bank statements, institutions), data DocuBite lacks (payment terms, discounts, buyers, entities), and anything that would reverse a #177 decision.

**Documented exceptions to Vic** (decided, do not re-open by "Vic wins ties"): the combined fields+source Detail pane (#179 → #224) with History as its tabs instead of Vic's left panel; the collapsible icon rail instead of Vic's top bar (#224 Q5); DocuBite's palette, type and emerald brand (this map, Q2); Exceptions as its own destination (#192); Touchless keeps its name.

**Settled while charting (grilled 2026-09-15):**

- **Scope is the whole operator app** — queues + Detail pane, Approvals inbox, PO matching in the row, Bill Pay + Payment Batches, Admin, mobile approval. One grammar everywhere.
- **Fidelity is grammar, not skin.** Same layouts, panels, chips, bars, keyboard flow, copy patterns; colour and type stay DocuBite's.
- **Payments never move money.** Bill Pay queue (open bills, terms, countdown, discounted amount over struck-through due) and Payment Batches queue (batch → approve → export file). The transfer stays outside DocuBite, as `preparePaymentRun` does today.
- **Approvals is a destination with two queues**, Invoices and PO Mismatches, each a personal Ready-to-Approve view with the sticky Approve/Reject bar. Exceptions stays separate.
- **Admin adopts Vic's full IA including Companies**: Configuration (per-field Editable/Required/Width, consequence toggles), Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies — one login, many companies, per-entity permissions. This is the one schema-and-auth effort on the map; it is researched before it is grilled.
- **Build order:** shell (#225) → distill (#238) → Approvals → PO matching → Payments → Admin → Mobile.
- **Removal protocol (owner's rule, #237):** nothing is removed from the app without the owner signing off each removal by name on the ticket. Removed features are *unplugged* (CONTEXT.md term), not deleted, so a return is a re-link.

name: docubite-local-db-access
description: "How to reach DocuBite's local Postgres from the agent sandbox when docker-compose's host port mapping isn't actually bound"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: cb136b9f-bc34-4b7b-8652-c14e7b2e664e
  modified: 2026-09-15T14:00:00.339Z
---

The `docubite-db-1` container (pgvector/pg17) is usually already running, but `docker port docubite-db-1` / the compose file's `55432:5432` mapping is not actually bound to the host in this sandbox — `localhost:55432` connection attempts fail with P1001 even though the container is healthy.

**Working fix:** the sandbox shares the Docker bridge network namespace, so the container's internal IP is directly reachable. Get the real DB password from the running web container (it's a generated secret, not the `docubite`/`docubite` placeholder in `docker-compose.yml`), and the container's bridge IP, then point `DATABASE_URL` at that IP with the real port 5432:

```bash
docker inspect docubite-db-1 --format '{{.NetworkSettings.Networks.docubite_default.IPAddress}}'
docker exec docubite-web-1 sh -c 'echo $DATABASE_URL'   # copy the password out of this
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://docubite:<real-password>@<db-container-ip>:5432/document_inbox"
npx prisma migrate dev / db execute / etc. now work directly from the repo checkout.
```

**Why:** `docubite-web-1` runs a stale prebuilt image with no source bind mount (only `document_sources`/`pgdata` volumes are mounted) — you can't run the app itself in that container, but you *can* reach its database directly this way to run migrations, seed data, or query state instead of assuming "no live DB in this sandbox," which several prior Wayfinder map #177 sessions incorrectly concluded.

**How to apply:** before flagging a "no live in-browser detector pass" or "no local Postgres" gap on this repo, try this connection method first — it may already resolve the blocker.

## Resolution

Grilled 2026-09-15 by the Wayfinder autopilot under the owner's standing delegation (every question answered with its `➡️` recommendation; the full rounds are in `docs/wayfinder-reports/226/229.md`). Skills run: `grilling`, `domain-modeling`, `intent` (context + `journey`), `impeccable shape`. Incumbent: the Invoices bulk-bar "Prepare payment run" → confirm → CSV download, with no home afterwards. Tour reference: `payments-bill-pay-discount.png`, `payments-batches-metric.png`, `payments-batch-detail-sheet.png` (§6 of `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md`). Incumbent critiques: the Finance seam 14/40 (`.impeccable/critique/2026-09-15T22-25-51Z__…finance…`, "payment run has no home after download", approval and payment eligibility disagree) and the fresh payment-run flow critique **13/40** (`.impeccable/critique/2026-09-15T23-16-19Z__invoices-prepare-payment-run-incumbent.md`; in-page detector bulk bar 6 @1440 · 7 @390, confirm open 11 · 11, shell baseline 5; three P0s: no approval gate, failures thrown to the outage screen, no home or receipt after the download; the static scan could not run unattended). Its pure-execution defects are listed on #251 to fix in the build.

### Decisions

1. **Payment batch, not payment run.** `payment_runs` is extended, not replaced, into the user-facing *Payment batch*: additive columns for name, comment, submitter, decision, export and paid facts, payer account and currency. `PaymentRunItem` keeps preventing double-batching.
2. **Lifecycle:** Pending approval → Approved → Paid; Rejected (reason required) is terminal and returns the invoices to Bill Pay. No persisted Draft — the Create batch dialog is the draft. **Downloading the file is a fact** (`exportedAt/By`, shown on the batch), never a state, so a phone can approve and a desktop can export later. Approve and Mark as paid are Server-confirmed writes; no optimistic removal, no Undo, no single-key approve (#227's rules carried over).
3. **Roles:** any member submits a batch (moves no money, needs approval); an owner approves, rejects, downloads and marks paid (#227's Approver rule for a stage that names nobody, until #231 can add a payments flow). Self-approval is allowed, labelled "You submitted this batch", both facts audited — a one-owner workspace must not dead-lock.
4. **Pay From = Payer account:** a named workspace bank account (name, bank, last four, currency, default) defined once under Settings › Payments. It labels the batch, the filename and the remittance advice and tells the uploader which portal to use; the file never carries its number. **One batch = one payer account = one currency = one file**; a mixed selection splits and the dialog says so.
5. **Payment terms and discount become Supplier fields:** `earlyPaymentDiscountPercent` + `earlyPaymentDiscountDays` beside the existing `paymentTermsDays`, rendered as Terms "2/10 net 30" (AP convention; Vic's "2-10-30" is skin). Discount applies while today ≤ invoice date + discount days; the purple *Expires in N days* countdown #188 held back now has real data. A supplier without terms shows "—" and no discount claim, ever.
6. **Mark as paid writes a Payment record** (amount, date, method batch|manual, batch, reference, who). Paid state is **derived, ledger first**: ledger confirms → Paid (ledger); records ≥ due → Paid (recorded); records < due → Partially paid; in a pending/approved batch → Scheduled; else Unpaid. Never pushed to the ledger here (#248 owns the push). Reversible via "Remove payment record" with a reason. ADR: `docs/adr/0001-paid-state-derived-from-ledger-then-payment-records.md`.
7. **Bill Pay membership:** processing state Approved, not cancelled, not fully paid (the approval gate #239 Q14 asked for; #249's in-place fix becomes this rule). Batched rows live under the *Scheduled* facet. An approved invoice whose supplier has no bank details is shown, undecidable, "Needs bank details" with a link to the supplier — today `preparePaymentRun` drops it silently.
8. **Open invoices by age** is Bill Pay's one metric, a band above the header band, buckets clicking into the filtered queue (tour lesson 10: the KPI where the actor lives; aging is the payer's question, Invoices keeps its Aging chip). **Early Payment Savings** appears on Payment Batches only once a supplier has discount terms — no empty KPI.
9. **IA:** one rail item **Payments** after Approvals, two queues `/payments/bill-pay` and `/payments/batches` (the #236 pattern), badge = batches pending my approval. "Prepare payment run" leaves the Invoices bulk bar; Invoices' Approve receipt says "Approved invoices are ready in Bill Pay".
10. **Bill Pay columns:** Supplier · Invoice # · Invoice date · Terms · Due + countdown · Bill total · Currency · Amount to pay (discounted over struck-through due, #188's inline-adjustment component) · Pay From. Est. arrival date and method dropped (no rails to estimate from). No processing-glyph column (every row is Approved). Amount to pay editable inline on desktop within 0 < amount ≤ due (partial payments are a real ledger condition); read-only on the phone. Bulk bar: Create batch · Mark as paid · Set Pay From.
11. **Payment Batches:** system views Pending approval · Approved · Paid, Rejected under Closed (documented exception: DocuBite has a real middle state Vic's Approve & Pay does not). Columns Created · Submitted by · Due (earliest in the batch; red countdown when overdue and still pending) · Batch name · Bills · Total · Currency · Pay From. Detail in the 60% Detail pane (exception to Vic's 78% sheet): summary strip, supplier-grouped lines, Audit tab, sticky Reject · Approve, then Download payment file · Mark batch as paid.
12. **States and copy:** Bill Pay empty "Nothing to pay. Approved invoices land here."; Batches empty "No batches yet. Select invoices in Bill Pay to create one."; failures inline in the pane footer with Retry. Countdown and discount badges only on real deadlines (no fabricated urgency).
13. **Rendering (Impeccable):** queue shell unchanged (Invoices baseline in-page 6/5); metric band 56px in DocuBite's skin using the aging palette already in `aging-summary.tsx`; discounted figure emerald-700 over slate-500 line-through with sr-only "was", never colour alone; Terms in tabular figures without accent; inline inputs 36px on desktop; below md Supplier · Amount to pay · Due per #235; tone quieter.
14. **Measure:** days approval → export; share overdue at batch creation; discount captured of available; counter-metric: payment records later contradicted by the ledger.

### Glossary (CONTEXT.md, committed)

Bill Pay · Payment batch · Payer account · Payment terms · Payment record; Invoice's entry now points paying at Bill Pay.

### Action Summary for the execution session

Intent: `specify` → `fortify` → `articulate` → `include`. Impeccable: `shape` → `layout` → `clarify` → `harden` → `adapt` → `audit` → `polish`.

### Tickets

- Execution: **#251** Build the Payments destination (sub-issue of #226, blocked by this ticket only).
- **#248** (Finance's shape) now also blocked by #251: it needs Bill Pay to exist.
- Fog added to the map: payments approval flow and payments role (after #231); SEPA and other file formats; Finance folding into Payments after #248. Fog graduated: Bill Pay's Open/Closed sub-states.

### Needs the owner (not decided here)

- Confirm the relocation of "Prepare payment run" off the Invoices bulk bar under the removal protocol (#237). It is a move, not a removal — the ticket question itself asks for the replacement — but it is named here so it can be vetoed before #251 builds it.

1	import { getCurrentUser } from "@/lib/auth"
2	import { listWorkspaceBills, type BillRow } from "@/models/bills"
3	import { getMinConfidencePercent } from "@/models/automation-config"
4	import { requireWorkspaceRole, type WorkspaceRole } from "@/models/workspaces"
5	import { listSavedViews } from "@/models/saved-views"
6	import { createSavedViewAction, deleteSavedViewAction, duplicateSavedViewAction, renameSavedViewAction, saveFiltersToViewAction, shareSavedViewAction } from "@/app/(app)/workspaces/[workspaceId]/(chrome)/saved-views-actions"
7	import { preparePaymentRunAction } from "@/app/(app)/workspaces/[workspaceId]/(chrome)/bills/actions"
8	import { InvoiceQueue } from "@/components/queue/invoice-queue"
9	import { QueueStat } from "@/components/queue/queue-stat"
10	import { SavedViewPicker } from "@/components/typed-destinations/saved-view-picker"
11	import { getTouchlessRateTrend } from "@/lib/analytics/workspace-analytics"
12	import type { AgingBucket } from "@/lib/bills/due-date"
13	
14	export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"
15	
16	export type InvoiceSearchParams = { blocked?: string; unpaid?: string; status?: string; approval?: string; touchless?: string; aging?: string; po?: string; view?: string; sort?: string }
17	
18	/** #225: Invoices on the Queue screen. Filters stay plain URL params (shareable, refreshable,
19	 * saveable as a view); the aging chip group filters here after the fetch since `agingBucket` is
20	 * derived per row, and the per-bucket totals now live on the Dashboard. */
21	export async function InvoicesQueuePage({ params, searchParams, selectedDocumentId = null }: {
22	  params: Promise<{ workspaceId: string }>
23	  searchParams: Promise<InvoiceSearchParams>
24	  selectedDocumentId?: string | null
25	}) {
26	  const { workspaceId } = await params
27	  const { blocked, unpaid, status, approval, touchless, aging, po, view: selectedViewId } = await searchParams
28	  const user = await getCurrentUser()
29	  const membership = await requireWorkspaceRole(workspaceId, user.id)
30	  const isOwner = membership.role === "owner"
31	
32	  const onlyBlocked = blocked === "1"
33	  const onlyUnpaid = unpaid === "1"
34	  const onlyTouchless = touchless === "1"
35	  const statusFilter = status === "unreviewed" || status === "reviewed" || status === "synced" || status === "paid" ? status : undefined
36	  const approvalFilter: BillRow["approvalStatus"] | undefined =
37	    approval === "not_started" || approval === "in_progress" || approval === "approved" || approval === "rejected" || approval === "cancelled" ? approval : undefined
38	  const agingFilter = new Set((aging ?? "").split(",").filter((value): value is AgingBucket | "none" => ["current", "1-30", "31-60", "61-90", "90+", "none"].includes(value)))
39	  const poFilter = po === "matched" || po === "none" || po === "mismatch" ? po : undefined
40	  const basePath = `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/invoices`
41	  const [{ bills: allBills }, minConfidencePercent, savedViews, touchlessTrend] = await Promise.all([
42	    listWorkspaceBills({ workspaceId, onlyBlocked, onlyUnpaid, statusFilter, approvalFilter, onlyTouchless, poFilter }),
43	    getMinConfidencePercent(workspaceId),
44	    listSavedViews({ workspaceId, viewKey: "invoices", userId: user.id }),
45	    getTouchlessRateTrend(workspaceId),
46	  ])
47	  const bills = agingFilter.size === 0 ? allBills : allBills.filter((bill) => agingFilter.has(bill.agingBucket ?? "none"))
48	  const currentViewFilters: Record<string, string> = {
49	    ...(onlyBlocked ? { blocked: "1" } : {}), ...(onlyUnpaid ? { unpaid: "1" } : {}),
50	    ...(onlyTouchless ? { touchless: "1" } : {}), ...(statusFilter ? { status: statusFilter } : {}),
51	    ...(approvalFilter ? { approval: approvalFilter } : {}), ...(agingFilter.size ? { aging: [...agingFilter].join(",") } : {}),
52	    ...(poFilter ? { po: poFilter } : {}),
53	  }
54	  // Only bills with a total AND an unblocked status are candidates for a payment run. #220: a
55	  // cancelled invoice is excluded too. "synced" (pushed but unconfirmed) stays eligible.
56	  const payableBills = bills.filter((b) => !b.blockedByCheck && !b.cancelledAt && b.total !== null && b.total > 0 && (!b.paymentStatus || !["paid", "reconciled"].includes(b.paymentStatus.toLowerCase())))
57	  const payableDocumentIds = isOwner ? payableBills.map((bill) => bill.documentId) : []
58	  const trend = touchlessTrend.trend ? `${touchlessTrend.trend.deltaPercentagePoints > 0 ? "+" : ""}${touchlessTrend.trend.deltaPercentagePoints}pt` : null
59	
60	  return <InvoiceQueue
61	    workspaceId={workspaceId}
62	    basePath={basePath}
63	    bills={bills}
64	    payableDocumentIds={payableDocumentIds}
65	    preparePaymentRunAction={preparePaymentRunAction.bind(null, workspaceId)}
66	    minConfidencePercent={minConfidencePercent}
67	    initialSelectedId={selectedDocumentId}
68	    stat={<QueueStat label="Touchless" value={`${Math.round(touchlessTrend.touchlessRate * 100)}%`}
69	      detail={`${touchlessTrend.totalPushedTouchless} of ${touchlessTrend.totalExtracted} sent without review, last 30 days${trend ? `, ${trend} vs. prior 30` : ""}`}
70	      trend={touchlessTrend.trend?.direction ?? null} />}
71	    views={<SavedViewPicker views={savedViews} selectedViewId={selectedViewId ?? null} currentFilters={currentViewFilters}
72	      currentUserId={user.id} currentUserRole={membership.role as WorkspaceRole}
73	      createAction={createSavedViewAction.bind(null, workspaceId, "invoices", basePath)}
74	      duplicateAction={duplicateSavedViewAction.bind(null, workspaceId, "invoices", basePath)}
75	      renameAction={renameSavedViewAction.bind(null, workspaceId, basePath)}
76	      saveFiltersAction={saveFiltersToViewAction.bind(null, workspaceId, basePath)}
77	      deleteAction={deleteSavedViewAction.bind(null, workspaceId, basePath)}
78	      shareAction={shareSavedViewAction.bind(null, workspaceId, basePath)} />} />
79	}
80	
81	export default function InvoicesPage({ params, searchParams }: { params: Promise<{ workspaceId: string }>; searchParams: Promise<InvoiceSearchParams> }) {
82	  return InvoicesQueuePage({ params, searchParams })
83	}

2	import { prisma } from "@/lib/db"
3	import { recordSystemAudit } from "@/lib/audit"
4	import { listWorkspaceBills } from "@/models/bills"
5	import { formatZaEftCsv, paymentRunFilename, totalsByCurrency, type PaymentInstruction } from "@/lib/payments/za-eft-csv"
6	import { buildRemittanceAdvices, type RemittanceAdvice } from "@/lib/payments/remittance"
7	import type { Prisma } from "@/prisma/client"
8	
9	export type PreparePaymentRunResult = {
10	  run: { id: string; filename: string; itemCount: number; totalsByCurrency: Record<string, number> }
11	  csv: string
12	  advices: RemittanceAdvice[]
13	}
14	
15	/** WP-AP2: prepares a payment run from the given bills for this workspace. Filters out bills
16	 * that are already in an active (non-cancelled) run so the same invoice isn't paid twice, and
17	 * returns the generated CSV + per-supplier remittance advices. Never itself moves money — the
18	 * user takes the CSV to their bank's own portal.
19	 *
20	 * Bills without a supplier bank account are dropped from the run rather than blocking it — the
21	 * caller renders the "N bills need a bank account" hint separately. */
22	export async function preparePaymentRun(input: {
23	  workspaceId: string
24	  actorId: string
25	  documentIds: string[]
26	  now?: Date
27	}): Promise<PreparePaymentRunResult> {
28	  const now = input.now ?? new Date()
29	  if (input.documentIds.length === 0) throw new Error("no_documents_selected")
30	
31	  const { bills } = await listWorkspaceBills({ workspaceId: input.workspaceId, limit: 1000 })
32	  const selectedIds = new Set(input.documentIds)
33	  const selected = bills.filter((b) => selectedIds.has(b.documentId))
34	
35	  const alreadyInRun = await prisma.paymentRunItem.findMany({
36	    where: { workspaceId: input.workspaceId, documentId: { in: input.documentIds }, active: true },
37	    select: { documentId: true },
38	  })
39	  const alreadyIds = new Set(alreadyInRun.map((r) => r.documentId).filter(Boolean) as string[])
40	
41	  const suppliers = await prisma.supplier.findMany({
42	    where: { workspaceId: input.workspaceId, id: { in: selected.map((b) => b.supplierId).filter((id): id is string => id !== null) } },
43	    select: { id: true, iban: true, bankDetails: true },
44	  })
45	  const bankBySupplier = new Map(suppliers.map((s) => {
46	    const details = (s.bankDetails ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>
47	    const account = typeof details.account === "string" ? details.account : (typeof details.iban === "string" ? details.iban : (typeof s.iban === "string" ? s.iban : null))
48	    const branchCode = typeof details.branchCode === "string" ? details.branchCode : (typeof details.branch === "string" ? details.branch : null)
49	    return [s.id, { account, branchCode }]
50	  }))
51	
52	  const instructions: PaymentInstruction[] = []
53	  const skipped: Array<{ documentId: string; reason: string }> = []
54	  for (const bill of selected) {
55	    if (alreadyIds.has(bill.documentId)) { skipped.push({ documentId: bill.documentId, reason: "already_in_active_run" }); continue }
56	    // #220: server-side defense in depth — the client already excludes a cancelled invoice from
57	    // payableDocumentIds, but a payment file is money leaving the workspace, so this doesn't rely
58	    // on that alone.
59	    if (bill.cancelledAt) { skipped.push({ documentId: bill.documentId, reason: "cancelled" }); continue }
60	    if (bill.total === null || bill.total <= 0) { skipped.push({ documentId: bill.documentId, reason: "missing_amount" }); continue }
61	    if (!bill.supplier) { skipped.push({ documentId: bill.documentId, reason: "missing_supplier" }); continue }
62	    const bank = bill.supplierId ? bankBySupplier.get(bill.supplierId) : null
63	    if (!bank?.account) { skipped.push({ documentId: bill.documentId, reason: "missing_bank_account" }); continue }
64	    instructions.push({
65	      documentId: bill.documentId,
66	      supplier: bill.supplier,
67	      bankAccountNumber: bank.account,
68	      branchCode: bank.branchCode ?? null,
69	      amount: bill.total,
70	      currencyCode: (bill.currencyCode ?? "ZAR").toUpperCase(),
71	      reference: bill.invoiceNumber ?? bill.documentId.slice(0, 8),
72	    })
73	  }
74	
75	  if (instructions.length === 0) throw new Error("no_payable_bills_after_filtering")
76	
77	  const csv = formatZaEftCsv(instructions)
78	  const filename = paymentRunFilename(now)
79	  const totals = totalsByCurrency(instructions)
80	
81	  const workspace = await prisma.workspace.findFirst({ where: { id: input.workspaceId }, select: { name: true } })
82	  const advices = buildRemittanceAdvices(instructions, { name: workspace?.name ?? "Your workspace", runDate: now })
83	
84	  const run = await prisma.paymentRun.create({
85	    data: {
86	      workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
87	      createdById: input.actorId,
88	      status: "draft",
89	      filename,
90	      itemCount: instructions.length,
91	      totalsJson: totals as unknown as Prisma.InputJsonValue,
92	      items: {
93	        create: instructions.map((ins) => ({
94	          workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
95	          documentId: ins.documentId,
96	          supplier: ins.supplier,
97	          amount: ins.amount,
98	          currencyCode: ins.currencyCode,
99	          reference: ins.reference,
100	        })),
101	      },
102	    },
103	    select: { id: true, filename: true, itemCount: true },
104	  })
105	
106	  await recordSystemAudit({
107	    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
108	    type: "payment_run_prepared",
109	    detail: { runId: run.id, itemCount: run.itemCount, skipped, totalsByCurrency: totals },
110	  })
111	
112	  return {
113	    run: { id: run.id, filename: run.filename ?? filename, itemCount: run.itemCount, totalsByCurrency: totals },
114	    csv,
115	    advices,
116	  }
117	}
118	
119	/** Marks a draft run as sent to the bank. Called from the "I've uploaded it" server action, so
120	 * the aging view knows not to keep flagging the bills as unpaid until the ledger sync catches
121	 * up. Ledger reconciliation itself is unchanged — bank-match matches the payment lines back to
122	 * these documents through their invoice references, exactly like it does today for manually-paid
123	 * bills. */
124	export async function markPaymentRunSent(input: { workspaceId: string; runId: string; actorId: string }) {
125	  const run = await prisma.paymentRun.findFirst({ where: { id: input.runId, workspaceId: input.workspaceId }, select: { id: true, status: true } })
126	  if (!run) throw new Error("payment_run_not_found")
127	  if (run.status !== "draft") throw new Error("payment_run_not_draft")
128	  const updated = await prisma.paymentRun.update({
129	    where: { id: run.id },
130	    data: { status: "sent", sentAt: new Date() },
131	    select: { id: true, status: true, sentAt: true },
132	  })
133	  await recordSystemAudit({
134	    workspaceId: input.workspaceId,
135	    type: "payment_run_sent",
136	    detail: { runId: run.id, actorId: input.actorId },
137	  })
138	  return updated
139	}
140	
141	export async function listPaymentRuns(workspaceId: string, opts: { limit?: number } = {}) {
142	  return prisma.paymentRun.findMany({
143	    where: { workspaceId },
144	    orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
145	    take: opts.limit ?? 50,
146	    select: { id: true, filename: true, status: true, itemCount: true, totalsJson: true, sentAt: true, createdAt: true },
147	  })
148	}

16

18	  if (!documentIds.length) throw new Error("no_documents_selected")
19	
20	  const { run } = await preparePaymentRun({ workspaceId, actorId: user.id, documentIds })
21	  revalidatePath(`/workspaces/${workspaceId}/bills`)
22	  redirect(`/api/workspaces/${workspaceId}/payment-runs/${run.id}/download`)
23	}

// Deliberately NOT a "use server" module: server actions live upstream and do the auth. This
// trusts the workspaceId it is handed.
import { prisma } from "@/lib/db"
import { agingBucket, inferDueDate, type AgingBucket } from "@/lib/bills/due-date"
import { getDocumentPaymentStatuses } from "@/models/ledger-payments"
import { normalizeSupplierName } from "@/lib/suppliers/normalize"
import type { PoLinkKind } from "@/lib/matching/po-link"
import { summarizeInvoicePoLinks, type InvoicePoSummary } from "@/models/po-matching"

/** WP-AP2: AP aging / bills cockpit. One row per Document whose template maps to "invoice" — the
 * shape an AP controller expects on day one: supplier, total, due-date (extracted OR inferred
 * from supplier payment terms), aging bucket, payment status from the ledger sync, and a flag
 * for "blocked by an open check". Everything is derived from data that already lives elsewhere;
 * this is a projection, not a new persisted table. */

export type BillRow = {
  documentId: string
  filename: string
  supplier: string | null
  supplierId: string | null
  total: number | null
  currencyCode: string | null
  invoiceNumber: string | null
  documentDate: Date | null
  extractedDueDate: Date | null
  dueDate: Date | null
  agingBucket: AgingBucket | null
  paymentStatus: string | null
  paidAmount: number | null
  /** When the ledger last confirmed this payment status — the closest thing to a "paid on" date
   * a synced push gives us (there's no separate payment-event table). Null until synced. */
  paidAt: Date | null
  status: string
  reviewedAt: Date | null
  blockedByCheck: boolean
  openCheckCodes: string[]
  /** Invoice Approval, per #211's filter-chip taxonomy. Derived from the document's most recent
   * ReviewTask: "approved" once resolved with no rejection, "rejected" once rejected, "in_progress"
   * while a task is being worked, "not_started" while one sits open/unclaimed, and "approved" by
   * default once the document itself is reviewed with no task at all (nothing left to approve).
   * #220: "cancelled" takes priority over all of the above once `cancelledAt` is set — a cancelled
   * invoice's ReviewTask history stops mattering to this taxonomy. */
  approvalStatus: "not_started" | "in_progress" | "approved" | "rejected" | "cancelled"
  /** #220: when this invoice was terminally cancelled (manual, reason-required, no un-cancel
   * affordance). Null for every non-cancelled invoice. */
  cancelledAt: Date | null
  cancelledReason: string | null
  /** When the document's most recent ReviewTask was opened, but only while it's still open/
   * in_review — null once it resolves (approved/rejected) or if there was never a ReviewTask.
   * #208's Review SLA countdown badge times its clock from this. */
  reviewTaskOpenedAt: Date | null
  /** #225: the id of that same open/in_review ReviewTask, so the Detail pane's Approve / Reject
   * bar can decide it directly. Null whenever `reviewTaskOpenedAt` is null. */
  openReviewTaskId: string | null
  /** Per-field extraction confidence (0-1), keyed the same as `reviewedData` ("vendor"/"merchant",
   * "total"/"amount", "invoice_number", "due_date"). Read from `document.confidence.fieldConfidence`
   * — #199/#219's row anatomy underlines every extracted-field cell from it; absent for a field
   * means no confidence was recorded (e.g. manually entered), not zero confidence. */
  fieldConfidence: Record<string, number>
  /** #200: whether this invoice's push went out with no human review — a `push.touchless_enqueued`
   * document-audit event exists for it. Drives the Touchless pill; there is no "pending" state (a
   * document either has the event or it doesn't, nothing to poll for). */
  touchless: boolean
  /** #223 (Wayfinder map #177): an open (not yet resolved) escalation exists on this document —
   * a `DocumentCheckResult` with `status: "escalated"` and `escalationStatus` null/open/in_review.
   * Folds into the row's Needs attention processing state; see `lib/documents/processing-state.ts`. */
  escalated: boolean
  /** #228 Q5/Q6/Q11 (#250): the invoice's Purchase Order link for the Purchase Orders column —
   * the compared PO's number carrying the number of red glyphs the pane will show, or a dashed
   * suggestion the matcher made that compares nothing until confirmed, or "PO removed". */
  po: BillPoLink
}

export type BillPoLink = {
  kind: PoLinkKind | null
  poNumber: string | null
  poDocumentId: string | null
  mismatchCount: number
  confidence: number | null
  suggestionCount: number

---
status: accepted
---

# An invoice's paid state is derived, ledger first, then DocuBite's own payment records

DocuBite prepares payment files and never moves money, so "paid" was only ever a fact the ledger sync reported (`models/ledger-payments.ts`); a workspace without a connected ledger could never mark anything paid, and a downloaded payment file left no trace on the invoice (#229, map #226). We decided that Mark as paid and a paid payment batch write **payment records** (an amount, a date, a method, an optional reference) on DocuBite's side, and that the invoice's paid state is **derived** at read time: the ledger's confirmation wins when it exists; otherwise the sum of payment records against the amount due decides Paid, Partially paid or Unpaid, and membership of a pending or approved batch reads as Scheduled. Payment records are never pushed to the ledger by this path — ledger placement stays the Finance push's job — so a record and a ledger line can disagree, and the row must say which source it is reading.

## Considered options

- **Store `paidAt` on the Document.** Rejected: no partial payments, no reversal trail, and it would silently overwrite the ledger's answer.
- **Only trust the ledger.** Rejected: most workspaces in the sandbox have no ledger connected, and a batch that was uploaded to the bank would still read Unpaid the following week ("did I already pay this?" had no answer, Finance critique 14/40).
- **Push a payment to the ledger on Mark as paid.** Rejected for this map: approval never publishes (#227) and the ledger hand-off is #248's decision.

## Consequences

- `BillRow.paymentStatus` grows a `source: "ledger" | "recorded"` alongside the derived state, and the queue pill says "Paid (recorded)" when the ledger has not confirmed.
- Removing a payment record needs a reason and an audit event; nothing else can flip Paid back to Unpaid.
- The ledger sync overriding a recorded payment is a counter-metric worth watching (measure, #229 Q17).
44:The typed destination for a bill received from a supplier. Absorbs the former Documents/Bills surface; aging is a filter chip and a saved view here, and paying an approved invoice happens on Bill Pay, not on this queue.

116:**Payment batch**:
120:**Payer account**:
124:**Payment terms**:

content.content:
**Not eligible**:
An Approval that is visible to its Approver but cannot be decided yet because a hard check failed or an escalation is open on the invoice. Never hidden, never overridable from Approvals; the reason is shown on the row.

**Approval notice**:
The one email an Approver gets when Approvals reach a stage they can decide: every eligible Approval that reached them since their last notice, never more than one an hour, none when nothing is new, and nothing about their own actions. It names the supplier and amount and opens the row (or Ready to Approve, when there are several); it never decides anything. A still-undecided Approval is nudged at most twice more. The person who started a run gets the same kind of notice only when it is sent back for review. Each person can switch it off in one click.
_Avoid_: Reminder (as the user-facing name), digest, alert, push, notification (as a badge count)

**Bill Pay**:
The queue of approved, unpaid invoices from which payment batches are created. An invoice reaches it only once its processing state is Approved; one that cannot be paid yet (no supplier bank details) stays visible with the reason.
_Avoid_: Payables, payment run (the queue), pay list

**Payment batch**:
A named set of approved invoices, one payer account and one currency, submitted by a member for an owner's decision. Pending approval, then Approved (its payment file can be downloaded), then Paid; or Rejected with a reason. Whether the file has been downloaded is a fact shown on the batch, not a state. A batch never moves money.
_Avoid_: Payment run, remittance (that is the advice sent to the supplier), transfer

**Payer account**:
A named workspace bank account a payment batch is to be paid from — a label that tells the uploader which bank portal the file belongs to. DocuBite never holds the account's credentials and the file never carries its number.
_Avoid_: Pay From (Vic's column label is fine on screen; the concept is the payer account), funding source, bank connection

**Payment terms**:
A supplier's net days and, when offered, an early-payment discount: the percent and the days within which it applies, shown as "2/10 net 30". A supplier without a discount shows no discount claim and no discount countdown.
_Avoid_: Terms code, "2-10-30"

**Payment record**:
A DocuBite-side fact that an amount was paid against an invoice on a date, by a batch or by hand (Mark as paid). An invoice's paid state is derived from the ledger when it confirms payment, otherwise from its payment records. A payment record can be removed with a reason.
_Avoid_: Mark as paid (the action, not the record), settlement, ledger payment (that is the ledger's own line)

**Company**:
The user-facing name for a team workspace in Admin and the switcher: one legal or financial entity with its own currency, tax jurisdiction, suppliers, ledger and members. "Workspace" remains the storage and address term. The auto-created personal workspace is shown as Personal, never as a company.
_Avoid_: Entity (Vic's word), tenant, client (that is who the company belongs to)

content.content: app/api/workspaces/[workspaceId]/payment-runs/[runId]/download/route.ts

1	import { getCurrentUser } from "@/lib/auth"
2	import { requireWorkspaceRole } from "@/models/workspaces"
3	import { prisma } from "@/lib/db"
4	import { formatZaEftCsv, type PaymentInstruction } from "@/lib/payments/za-eft-csv"
5	import { decimalToNumber } from "@/lib/money"
6	import { notFound } from "next/navigation"
7	
8	/** GET /api/workspaces/<workspaceId>/payment-runs/<runId>/download — regenerates the ZA EFT CSV
9	 * for a prepared run and returns it as an attachment. The CSV is not stored on the run row (a
10	 * regenerated file is byte-identical), keeping the persisted state small.
11	 *
12	 * Auth: workspace member. Payment-run creation itself is owner-only (see the server action) but
13	 * anyone with workspace access can re-download the file — a member handling the actual bank
14	 * upload is the exact use case the run row exists to support. */
15	export async function GET(_req: Request, { params }: { params: Promise<{ workspaceId: string; runId: string }> }) {
16	  const { workspaceId, runId } = await params
17	  const user = await getCurrentUser()
18	  await requireWorkspaceRole(workspaceId, user.id)
19	
20	  const run = await prisma.paymentRun.findFirst({
21	    where: { id: runId, workspaceId },
22	    select: {
23	      id: true, filename: true,
24	      items: {
25	        where: { active: true },
26	        select: {
27	          documentId: true, supplier: true, amount: true, currencyCode: true, reference: true,
28	          document: {
29	            select: {
30	              reviewedData: true,
31	              // Bank details come from the resolved Supplier row via document.template? — but we
32	              // stashed the essentials on the item at creation. Only supplier bank fields matter
33	              // per row, so fetch them by name below (rather than re-resolving through aliases,
34	              // which would double the query without changing results in the common case).
35	            },
36	          },
37	        },
38	      },
39	    },
40	  })
41	  if (!run) notFound()
42	
43	  // Look up current supplier bank details by canonical name — refetched here so an updated bank
44	  // account since the run was created is reflected in the freshly-regenerated file.
45	  const suppliers = await prisma.supplier.findMany({
46	    where: { workspaceId, canonicalName: { in: run.items.map((i) => i.supplier) } },
47	    select: { canonicalName: true, iban: true, bankDetails: true },
48	  })
49	  const bankByName = new Map(suppliers.map((s) => {
50	    const details = (s.bankDetails ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>
51	    const account = typeof details.account === "string" ? details.account : (typeof details.iban === "string" ? details.iban : (typeof s.iban === "string" ? s.iban : null))
52	    const branchCode = typeof details.branchCode === "string" ? details.branchCode : (typeof details.branch === "string" ? details.branch : null)
53	    return [s.canonicalName, { account, branchCode }]
54	  }))
55	
56	  const instructions: PaymentInstruction[] = run.items.map((item) => {
57	    const bank = bankByName.get(item.supplier) ?? null
58	    return {
59	      documentId: item.documentId ?? "",
60	      supplier: item.supplier,
61	      bankAccountNumber: bank?.account ?? null,
62	      branchCode: bank?.branchCode ?? null,
63	      amount: decimalToNumber(item.amount) ?? 0,
64	      currencyCode: item.currencyCode,
65	      reference: item.reference,
66	    }
67	  })
68	
69	  const csv = formatZaEftCsv(instructions)
70	  const filename = run.filename ?? `payment-run-${runId}.csv`
71	  return new Response(csv, {
72	    status: 200,
73	    headers: {
74	      "content-type": "text/csv; charset=utf-8",
75	      "content-disposition": `attachment; filename="${filename}"`,
76	      "cache-control": "private, no-store",
77	    },
78	  })
79	}

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/ubuntu/Dev/Wes-doc/.claude/skills/intent

# Intent

## Invocation banner

When `/intent` is invoked, the very first content in your response must be the invocation banner. Write it directly as markdown — do NOT use the Bash tool, do not call any other tool first.

Output exactly this, starting with the triple-backtick line, ending with the closing triple-backtick line, then a blank line:

`````
```
◆ ─ │ ─ ─ ─ │ ─ ─ ─ ─ │ ─ ─ ─ │ ─ ─ │ ─ │ ─ ─ │ ─ ◆

  intent.

  Make the reason behind every decision visible.

  What are you designing, and for whom?

◆ ─ │ ─ ─ ─ │ ─ ─ ─ ─ │ ─ ─ ─ │ ─ ─ │ ─ │ ─ ─ │ ─ ◆
```
`````

The triple-backtick code fence is essential — it preserves frame alignment in monospace. Do not modify the content, do not paraphrase, do not skip the banner.

After the banner renders, continue with the rest of this skill's normal response.

## Overview

Intent is a UX and design strategy system. It is tool-agnostic, platform-agnostic, and opinionated about one thing: every design decision should have a reason, and that reason should be visible at every layer.

Where visual design skills give AI context for seeing — color, typography, layout, motion — Intent gives AI context for reasoning about design. For asking why before how. For framing problems before solving them. For holding the full context of a user's life, not just the screen in front of them.

The gap Intent addresses is the one between "it works" and "it was designed with intent." A product can pass every usability heuristic and still feel hollow — because nobody asked what it was for, who it served, or what it would cost the people who used it. Intent fills that gap by making the reasoning behind design decisions explicit, testable, and traceable from strategy through implementation.

**What Intent is:**
- A thinking system for UX decisions, grounded in research and ethics
- A routing layer that connects specialized design skills into coherent practice
- An anti-pattern defense that makes manipulative design visible and refusable
- A context-gathering protocol that establishes shared understanding before work begins

**What Intent is not:**
- A visual design system
- A UI component library
- A substitute for primary user research
- A set of rules to follow blindly — it's a set of questions to ask rigorously

**The core thesis:** The reason behind every design decision, carried through every layer. Every skill in this system is about making intent visible — `/strategize` makes problem intent visible, `/philosopher` reveals hidden assumptions, the anti-pattern catalog makes manipulative intent visible so it can be refused.

## When NOT to use Intent

Intent adds rigor. Rigor is valuable when it's the scarce resource and costly when it's not. Skip Intent when:

- **The task is a localized tweak within an established system.** Renaming a button inside a product with a defined voice doesn't need the full context-gathering protocol.
- **The task is purely technical with no user-facing change.** Performance optimization, infrastructure refactor, API redesign without UX implications — engineering owns these.
- **A different framework is the right tool.** Brand identity belongs to creative direction. Visual component systems belong to design-system tooling. Intent is not a hammer for every nail.
- **Time pressure makes rigor a net negative.** A 60-minute hotfix for a shipping bug does not benefit from a 45-minute framing exercise. Ship the fix, note the debt, return to it.
- **The user has explicit expertise and a specific ask.** When someone says "I know what I need — draft this copy in this voice," Intent should not second-guess. Offer to flag risks if anything looks concerning, then produce.

If in doubt, ask once. Intent is a system that serves practice, not a gate that blocks it.

## Modes

Intent operates in three modes. Each establishes a different relationship to the work.

### `context` — Set project context

Use this mode at the start of any design engagement. Before any skill can do meaningful work, it needs to understand:

1. **Who are the users?** Not demographics — behaviors, contexts, motivations, constraints. A "25-34 year old professional" tells you nothing. "Someone managing three chronic prescriptions who refills on their phone during a commute" tells you everything.
2. **What is the product and business context?** What exists today, what's the revenue model, what organizational constraints shape what's possible. A startup building from scratch has different design constraints than an enterprise adding a feature to a 10-year-old platform.
3. **What are the hard constraints?** Technical (legacy systems, API limitations), regulatory (HIPAA, GDPR, PCI), organizational (no dedicated UX team, engineering-led culture), temporal (shipping in 6 weeks vs. 6 months).
4. **What is the ethical stance?** Every product makes ethical choices — explicitly or by default. Context mode makes them explicit. Are we opt-in or opt-out? Do we use engagement metrics or wellbeing metrics? Do we design for vulnerable populations or exclude them? Do we use persuasive patterns or informative ones?
5. **What does success look like?** Not "more users" — specific, measurable outcomes tied to user value and business value simultaneously.

Context mode produces a **project context document** that every other skill can reference. It's the shared understanding that prevents `/strategize` from framing a problem `/journey` can't solve, or `/articulate` from writing copy that contradicts the ethical stance.

### `practice` — Build and improve UX

This is the active design mode. Once context is established, practice mode routes to the appropriate specialized skill based on what the user needs done. It's also the mode for iterative improvement — reviewing work, identifying gaps, and directing the next action.

Practice mode follows this cycle:
1. **Assess** — What's the current state? Use `/evaluate` to understand quality.
2. **Identify** — Where are the gaps? What needs attention first?
3. **Route** — Which specialized skill addresses the highest-priority gap?
4. **Execute** — Do the work within the specialized skill.
5. **Verify** — Did the work address the gap? Are there new gaps?

The routing logic (detailed below) determines which skill to engage. Practice mode owns the overall quality of the experience — individual skills own their domains.

### `extract` — Extract UX patterns from an existing product

Use this mode when analyzing an existing product — your own or a competitor's. Extract mode systematically identifies:

- **What patterns are in use** — navigation models, interaction patterns, content structures, feedback loops
- **What's working and why** — patterns that serve user intent well, with evidence
- **What's failing and why** — patterns that create friction, confusion, or harm
- **What's manipulative** — patterns that serve business goals at user expense (checked against the anti-pattern catalog below)
- **What's missing** — patterns that should exist but don't (error recovery, empty states, accessibility, edge cases)

Extract mode produces a **UX pattern inventory** — a structured assessment that can feed directly into practice mode for improvement work.

## Core UX Principles

These are not visual principles. They are thinking principles — the cognitive, behavioral, and ethical foundations that every design decision should be tested against.

### 1. Respect user autonomy

The user is not a conversion target. They are a person making choices. Design should expand their ability to choose well, not constrain it.

**In practice:**
- No manipulation. No trick questions, hidden options, or shame-based copy. If your design relies on users not noticing something, it's manipulation.
- Clear choices. Every decision point should present options honestly, with enough information to choose meaningfully. "Are you sure?" is not informed consent.
- Easy reversal. Any action a user takes should be reversible wherever possible. Undo is not a feature — it's a right. Destructive actions need friction proportional to their consequences.
- Transparent consequences. Before a user acts, they should understand what will happen. After they act, they should see that it happened. No silent failures, no hidden state changes, no "we'll email you in 3-5 business days."

### 2. Design for real conditions

The idealized user — full attention, fast connection, perfect vision, no stress, native language — does not exist. Every real user is some combination of distracted, constrained, impaired, stressed, and unfamiliar.

**In practice:**
- Slow networks. Design for 3G before 5G. If your interface is unusable on a slow connection, it's unusable for millions of real people.
- Distraction. Users are interrupted. They switch tabs. They come back 20 minutes later. Your flow should survive that.
- Disability. Not an edge case — a spectrum everyone moves along. Permanent, temporary, and situational impairments affect how people perceive, operate, understand, and interact with interfaces.
- Stress. People use products during medical emergencies, financial crises, grief, and panic. Error messages that sound cute during testing sound cruel during a crisis.
- Unfamiliar language. Not everyone reads your interface in their first language. Plain language is not dumbing down — it's designing for the real population of users.
- Old devices. Not everyone has the latest phone. Design for the device your least privileged user actually owns.

### 3. Make intent visible

Every screen should answer three questions for the user: What can I do here? Why should I? What happens next?

**In practice:**
- Wayfinding. Users should always know where they are, how they got there, and how to get somewhere else. Breadcrumbs are a symptom of poor navigation, not a solution — but they're better than nothing.
- Purpose clarity. Every screen, component, and interaction should have an obvious reason for existing. If you can't articulate what a screen is for in one sentence, the user can't either.
- Progressive disclosure. Show what's needed now, reveal what's needed next. Don't hide things — sequence them. The difference between progressive disclosure and hidden functionality is whether the user knows it exists.
- Feedback loops. Every user action should produce visible feedback. Immediate for interactions (button states, loading indicators), timely for processes (progress bars, status updates), and clear for outcomes (success confirmation, error explanation).

### 4. Evidence over intuition

Research, test, measure. Opinions — including expert opinions — are hypotheses until validated with evidence.

**In practice:**
- Research before design. Understand the problem space before proposing solutions. Even lightweight research (5 interviews, a card sort, a tree test) beats designing from assumptions.
- Test with real users. Usability testing is not optional. Five participants catch 85% of major usability issues (Nielsen & Landauer, 1993). There is no excuse for shipping untested flows.
- Measure what matters. Metrics should track user success, not just business extraction. Task completion rate tells you more about UX quality than time-on-page.
- Acknowledge uncertainty. Say "we believe" instead of "we know." Flag sample sizes. Note when evidence is directional vs. conclusive. Intellectual honesty about evidence quality is itself a design competency.

### 5. Systems over screens

A screen is not a design. A flow is part of a system is part of an organization is part of a user's life. Design at the right altitude.

**In practice:**
- End-to-end thinking. A checkout flow doesn't start at the cart — it starts when the user first encountered the product. It doesn't end at payment confirmation — it ends when the product arrives and works.
- Cross-channel awareness. Users move between devices, channels, and contexts. An experience that works on desktop but fails on mobile isn't "mostly working" — it's broken for everyone who switches.
- Organizational awareness. Many UX problems are org chart problems in disguise. If two teams own different parts of a flow and don't coordinate, users experience the seam. Design can smooth seams, but acknowledging they exist is step one.
- Temporal awareness. Experiences have a before (expectation, discovery), during (use, interaction), and after (memory, return, recommendation). Most design focuses on "during" and ignores the other two.

### 6. Ethical defaults

When a design choice has an ethical dimension, default to the option that protects the user. Always.

**In practice:**
- Opt-in over opt-out. Don't pre-check boxes. Don't default to maximum data collection. Don't assume consent. Ask, and make "no" as easy as "yes."
- Privacy by default. Collect the minimum data needed. Store it securely. Delete it when it's no longer needed. Don't make privacy a premium feature.
- Honest over persuasive. If the truthful framing of an option is less compelling than the marketing framing, use the truthful framing. Urgency that doesn't exist ("Only 2 left!") is a lie. Scarcity that's manufactured is manipulation.
- Protect vulnerable populations. Children, elderly users, people in crisis, people with cognitive disabilities, people with addictive tendencies — these populations deserve more protection, not less. Design for their safety first.
